edges.target_label: Neuro-JEPA: Learning a Sparse Latent Predictive Foundation Model for Multimodal Neuroimaging (2026)
edges.note: Where MAE theory explained why masked reconstruction works, Neuro-JEPA swaps reconstruction for prediction in a learned latent space, because reconstructing raw neuroimaging spends capacity on noise.

edges.source_label: Self-supervised Learning for HAR with 700K Person-days (Yuan 2024)
edges.target_label: Neuro-JEPA: Learning a Sparse Latent Predictive Foundation Model for Multimodal Neuroimaging (2026)
edges.note: Where SSL for HAR scaled masked self-supervised pretraining on 700K person-days of sensor data, Neuro-JEPA keeps the large-scale pretraining but moves the objective to latent prediction with a sparsity constraint.

edges.target_label: Neuro-JEPA: Learning a Sparse Latent Predictive Foundation Model for Multimodal Neuroimaging (2026)
edges.note: Neuro-JEPA sits near the biosignal foundation-model survey as a biosignal effort, but on the latent-predictive rather than reconstructive branch.

edges.target_label: Visual Contrastive Self-Distillation (VCSD, 2026)
edges.note: Where DINO builds its teacher-student asymmetry from two augmented crops of one image, VCSD builds the asymmetry from input conditioning, original image versus content-erased image under a fixed text prefix, because for a vision-language model the useful signal is which tokens the image content raises.

edges.source_label: Self-supervised Learning for HAR with 700K Person-days (Yuan 2024)
edges.target_label: Visual Contrastive Self-Distillation (VCSD, 2026)
edges.note: Where SSL for HAR learned label-free sensor representations at scale, VCSD offers a label-free target built from full-input versus masked-control contrast that could transfer to channel-masked or band-masked sensor windows.
